facts.big: I’m saving. I’m going to deposit.
facts.label: Present continuous e going to
facts.sub: Use am/is/are + -ing para agora e going to + verbo para planos: I’m saving for a trip, I’m going to deposit money.

facts.label: estar + -ando
facts.sub: Use am/is/are + verbo-ing para o que acontece agora ou nesta fase: I’m saving for a trip. She is working on Saturdays. Para negar, use not: I’m not spending much.

facts.label: ir + verbo
facts.sub: Use going to para planos: I’m going to deposit two hundred dollars. Depois de going to vem o verbo base, sem to extra: She is going to buy a flight.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “estou juntando dinheiro” e “vou depositar”.
compare.us: Em inglês, use o present continuous para o que acontece agora ou nesta fase (I’m saving) e going to para planos (I’m going to deposit). Não esqueça o verbo be: I am, you are, she is.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: I’m saving for a trip.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: I’m saving for a trip means I am putting money aside now.
Going to is only for the past.
items.why: Going to is for plans and the future.

items.s: A budget helps you plan your money.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: I’m saving for a trip means I am putting money aside now. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Going to is only for the past. → Falso (Going to is for plans and the future.)
A budget helps you plan your money. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A savings plan in Sydney · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm morning in Sydney. Nina walks into a bank near the harbour. She is carrying a small notebook. Dawn works at the desk by the window. Nina is going to start a new plan. She is saving money for a long trip.

“Hi Nina! You look happy today. What are you doing at the bank?” says Dawn. “I’m opening a savings account. I’m saving for a trip to Bali.” says Nina. “Nice! Are you going to save every month, or only sometimes?” says Dawn.
